name: Poke Bowl
baseOrder: Half rice, half greens or cabbage base
Salmon or tuna
Edamame
Cucumber
Seaweed
Avocado
Shredded carrot & cabbage
Ponzu or light soy sauce on the side
Skip the shrimp — ask staff about cross-contamination with shellfish
whyItWorks: Fish and edamame bring in real protein without saturated fat
Vegetables add fiber that helps carry cholesterol out of your system
Avocado is a heart-healthy fat, not a scary one
Lighter on refined carbs than a full rice bowl
modifications: Ask for sauce on the side so you control how much goes on
Swap in extra greens if you want more volume without more rice
Add a scoop of extra edamame for more protein
watchOuts: Poke sauces and seaweed salad often have added sugar and sodium
Easy to end up with two or three sauces, which adds up fast
Double-check with staff about shrimp cross-contamination on shared prep surfaces
dentalTip: Rinse with water after eating — sticky sauces cling to teeth more than you'd think.
cholesterolTip: This bowl is already a solid cholesterol-friendly choice thanks to the fish and fiber. Ease up on any creamy or spicy-mayo toppings if offered.

name: Bagel with Lox
baseOrder: Whole grain or everything bagel over plain white if you have the option
A thin layer of cream cheese, or swap half for avocado
Smoked salmon
Capers, red onion, tomato, cucumber
Skip the second smear of cream cheese if you already added avocado
whyItWorks: Salmon brings omega-3 fats that support your lipid panel
Whole grain bread adds fiber a plain white bagel skips
Capers and onion add flavor without needing more fat
modifications: Ask for a thin scrape of cream cheese instead of a full layer
Half avocado, half light cream cheese keeps the flavor without doubling the saturated fat
Add tomato and cucumber for volume and fiber
watchOuts: Full-fat cream cheese is a meaningful saturated fat source if piled on
Refined white bagels spike blood sugar faster than whole grain
Lox can be salty, especially paired with capers
dentalTip: Bagels are chewy and can lodge in back teeth — a quick water swish after helps, especially with your cavity history.
cholesterolTip: The salmon here is genuinely great for your LDL/ApoB. The cream cheese amount is the one lever worth adjusting.

name: Vietnamese Rice Bowl
baseOrder: Grilled lemongrass chicken, pork, or tofu
Steamed jasmine or brown rice (ask for brown if it's offered)
Pickled carrots & daikon (đồ chua)
Cucumber and fresh herbs
Fish sauce or nước chấm on the side
Skip the fried spring roll add-on if you want it lighter
whyItWorks: Grilled protein instead of fried keeps saturated fat lower
Pickled vegetables add fiber and a lot of flavor for very little effort
Herbs and citrus notes make it feel like more than "diet food"
modifications: Ask for grilled instead of fried protein if there's a choice
Get sauce on the side — nước chấm can be sneaky sweet and salty
Add extra pickled vegetables instead of extra rice
watchOuts: Fried spring rolls or crispy pork add saturated fat fast
Nước chấm has sugar and fish sauce, both add up in sodium
Restaurant portions can run large — boxing half for later isn't a failure
dentalTip: Pickled vegetables are acidic — a sip of water afterward helps rebalance your mouth, especially with recent cavities.
cholesterolTip: Grilled lean protein plus fiber-rich pickled vegetables is a genuinely strong combo for your LDL/ApoB goals.

name: Pho
baseOrder: Broth with lean beef (well-done cuts), chicken, or tofu
Rice noodles — ask for a smaller noodle portion if you want more broth-to-veg ratio
Bean sprouts, Thai basil, lime, jalapeño mixed in
Go easy on hoisin and sriracha — add a little at a time
A side of extra vegetables if it's offered
whyItWorks: Broth-based soups are naturally lower in saturated fat than fried options
Lean beef or chicken plus herbs gives you protein without heaviness
Warm and steady — a great match for a tired or low-energy day
modifications: Choose leaner cuts over fattier ones when there's a choice
Add extra bean sprouts and herbs for fiber and crunch
Go light on hoisin sauce, which is high in sugar and sodium
watchOuts: Pho broth is high in sodium, especially at restaurants
Hoisin and sriracha both add sugar and sodium fast if free-poured
Rice noodles are a refined carb — the herbs and veggies help balance that
dentalTip: The broth is hot and can be acidic with lime — rinse with plain water after to protect enamel.
cholesterolTip: Lean protein choice matters most here. Let the broth, not fatty cuts, be where the richness comes from.

name: Salad Bowl
baseOrder: A big base of leafy greens, not just iceberg
Grilled chicken, salmon, chickpeas, or tofu for protein
A mix of colorful vegetables — the more colors, the more fiber
Nuts or seeds for healthy fat and crunch
Dressing on the side, vinaigrette over creamy or ranch
whyItWorks: Leafy greens and mixed vegetables are some of the best soluble-fiber sources for lowering LDL
A real protein portion keeps you full instead of snacky an hour later
Nuts and seeds add heart-healthy fat without needing creamy dressing
modifications: Swap creamy dressing for vinaigrette, or ask for it on the side
Add beans or lentils for extra fiber if the protein feels light
Skip the fried toppings (wonton strips, bacon bits) most of the time
watchOuts: Salads can quietly get high in sodium once cheese, bacon, and creamy dressing pile on
A salad with no real protein will leave you hungry within the hour
Croutons and candied nuts add sugar and refined carbs fast
dentalTip: Crunchy vegetables are great for your teeth. Just rinse with water after if the dressing was citrus-based.
cholesterolTip: This is one of the most reliably cholesterol-friendly options on any menu. Dressing choice is the one thing worth being picky about.

name: Matcha Drink
baseOrder: Matcha with oat, soy, or low-fat milk
Ask for less syrup — or half the usual pump count
Unsweetened or lightly sweetened over the standard sweet version
Enjoy it in one sitting rather than sipping for hours
whyItWorks: Matcha has antioxidants and a gentler caffeine curve than coffee — steadier energy, less of a crash
Plant milk keeps saturated fat low if you skip whole milk versions
A satisfying ritual that doesn't require a full meal to feel good
modifications: Ask for half sweetener — most shops default to quite sweet
Oat or soy milk over whole milk if you want it lighter
Add a splash of extra matcha if you want more flavor without more sugar
watchOuts: Standard sweetened matcha lattes can have as much sugar as a dessert
Sipping a sweet drink slowly over hours is harder on teeth than drinking it in one sitting
Some shops use flavored syrups with more sugar than the matcha itself
dentalTip: This is the one to watch most closely with your cavity history: drink it in one sitting rather than sipping for hours, and rinse with water after.
cholesterolTip: Matcha itself is cholesterol-neutral to mildly favorable. The milk and sweetener choice is what shifts it either direction.

name: Sushi
baseOrder: Sashimi or nigiri (salmon, tuna, yellowtail) over heavy rolls
A cucumber or avocado roll for lighter carbs
Edamame or seaweed salad on the side
Soy sauce lightly — wasabi and ginger for flavor, not a sodium habit
Skip shrimp/ebi and imitation crab — ask about shared prep surfaces for cross-contact
whyItWorks: Sashimi and nigiri are close to pure lean protein and healthy fat, very little refined carb
Edamame adds plant protein and fiber
Naturally lower sodium than fried or heavily sauced rolls
modifications: Choose nigiri or sashimi over tempura or spicy mayo rolls when possible
Ask for sauce or spicy mayo on the side instead of drizzled on
Add a cucumber roll instead of a second fried roll for volume
watchOuts: Fried rolls (tempura, crunch rolls) and spicy mayo add saturated fat and calories fast
Soy sauce is very high in sodium — a little goes a long way
Double-check shrimp and imitation crab (often contains shellfish) given your allergy
dentalTip: Pickled ginger is acidic — fine in small amounts, just rinse with water afterward rather than sipping soy-sauce-dipped bites over a long meal.
cholesterolTip: Sashimi-forward orders are some of the best cholesterol-friendly restaurant food that exists. Fried rolls are where that stops being true.

name: Lentil Soup
baseOrder: A bowl of lentil soup as the base
A squeeze of lemon and fresh herbs if available
A small piece of whole grain bread if you want something to chew
A side salad if you want more volume and fiber
whyItWorks: Lentils are one of the best soluble-fiber foods for actively lowering LDL cholesterol
Plant protein plus fiber keeps you full for hours — great for steady energy
Warm and low-effort, easy to make in a big batch and reheat all week
modifications: Add extra vegetables (carrots, spinach) to boost fiber and volume for free
A drizzle of olive oil adds good fat without tipping into heavy
Pair with whole grain bread instead of white for extra fiber
watchOuts: Canned or restaurant versions can be higher in sodium than homemade
Cream-based lentil soups lose most of the cholesterol benefit — go for broth-based
Bread on the side adds up if it's more than one slice
dentalTip: Soft and easy on teeth — one of the more dental-friendly meals here. Still worth a water rinse if bread or fruit is alongside.
cholesterolTip: This might be the single best food on this list for your LDL-C and ApoB specifically. Lentils are genuinely great here.

name: Tofu Bowl
baseOrder: Pan-seared or baked tofu (not deep-fried) as the protein
Brown rice, or half rice / half greens
Roasted or steamed vegetables — broccoli, carrots, bok choy
A light sesame-soy or peanut-lime sauce, on the side
Sesame seeds or crushed peanuts for texture
whyItWorks: Tofu is a complete plant protein with zero cholesterol and low saturated fat
Roasted vegetables add fiber and make the bowl feel substantial without more rice
A genuinely great post-walk refuel that won't sit heavy
modifications: Ask for tofu pan-seared or baked instead of fried when ordering out
Half rice, half greens if you want to lighten the carb load
Add extra vegetables instead of extra sauce for more volume
watchOuts: Fried tofu absorbs a lot of oil — nice texture, but it changes the nutrition profile a lot
Peanut and sesame sauces are easy to over-pour — ask for it on the side
Some sauces are surprisingly high in sugar (teriyaki especially)
dentalTip: A gentle, non-acidic meal overall — a good choice on a day your teeth feel sensitive.
cholesterolTip: Tofu is one of the most direct swaps for animal protein if you're working on LDL/ApoB — it genuinely does the job here.

name: Salmon Rice Bowl
baseOrder: Grilled or baked salmon (skip crispy-fried-in-oil versions most days)
Half rice / half greens, or a full vegetable base
Avocado, cucumber, edamame, shredded carrot
A light soy-sesame or citrus dressing, on the side
A sprinkle of sesame seeds or seaweed flakes
whyItWorks: Salmon is one of the best omega-3 sources, which directly supports your lipid panel
Balanced macros — real protein, fiber from vegetables, healthy fat from fish and avocado
Filling enough to actually carry you through the afternoon
modifications: Ask for salmon grilled or baked rather than crispy-fried if ordering out
Add extra greens instead of extra rice for more volume and fiber
Go light on sweet glazes (teriyaki-style), which add sugar fast
watchOuts: Sweet glazes and teriyaki sauces add sugar quickly — ask for sauce on the side
Portions at some fast-casual spots run large on rice specifically — half rice half greens fixes this
Watch sodium if the salmon is heavily seasoned or the sauce is soy-based
dentalTip: A low-risk meal for your teeth overall. If the glaze is sweet, a water rinse after is a good habit.
cholesterolTip: This is close to an ideal cholesterol-supportive meal already — the fish and fiber are doing real work for your LDL/ApoB.
